name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
venue: ICLR 2026 (The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations; OpenReview id jL7fwchScm). Preprint arXiv:2509.25140 (cs.AI/cs.CL), submitted 29 Sep 2025 (v1), last revised 16 Mar 2026 (v2).

maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/google-research/reasoning-bank (Apache-2.0; releases code for WebArena and SWE-Bench; OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=jL7fwchScm)
task_domain: LLM-agent sequential decision-making in interactive environments: web browsing (WebArena, Mind2Web) and software engineering / repository-level issue resolution (SWE-Bench-Verified). Spans web and code agent domains.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, gradient-free test-time learning. A stream of task queries Q={q1..qN} arrives sequentially and must be solved one at a time without access to future queries and WITHOUT any ground-truth labels at test time (proxy correctness comes from an LLM-as-a-Judge). The agent policy is a backbone LLM (Gemini-2.5-Flash/Pro, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, also Gemma-3-12B) conditioned on a memory module M (ReasoningBank), initialized empty, acting via a ReAct-style loop over web-navigation operations (BrowserGym, max 30 steps) or bash commands (mini-SWE-Agent, bash-only). The agent must self-evolve across the stream by extracting and reusing memory from its own past successful AND failed trajectories. Supervision: no test-time ground truth; an LLM-as-a-Judge (same backbone, temperature 0.0) provides binary success/failure signals. A second contribution, memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS), allocates more inference compute per task (parallel: multiple rollouts; sequential: iterative self-refinement) with scaling factor k.
what_is_retrieved: Self-distilled reasoning-strategy memory items extracted from the agent's own past successful and failed experiences. Each item is a structured unit with (i) a title (concise strategy identifier), (ii) a one-sentence description, and (iii) content recording distilled reasoning steps, decision rationales, or operational insights/pitfalls. These are generalizable reasoning strategies and guardrails, NOT raw trajectories or success-only workflows.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic self-written memory: ReasoningBank starts empty and is populated online during the test-time stream from the agent's own trajectories (both successes and failures). No static external corpus/KB/API store; the retrievable store is entirely self-generated and grows during deployment (closed-loop retrieve -> extract -> consolidate).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: the agent retrieves the top-k most relevant past experiences (and their associated memory items) by embedding similarity. There is no minimal-complete-set or variable-size precision-driven objective. The number-of-retrieved-experiences ablation (WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash) finds k=1 best (49.7), with success rate declining as k grows (46.0 at k=2, 45.5 at k=3, 44.4 at k=4), so the default uses a small fixed k (k=1 in the ablated best setting).
retrieval_unit: guideline-rule / distilled reasoning-strategy memory item (title + description + content). Retrieval is keyed on past experiences; each retrieved experience carries its associated structured memory items (high-level transferable reasoning patterns), not full raw trajectories or executable programs.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced: the retrievable store is built incrementally during the streaming test-time evaluation from the agent's own successful and failed trajectories (distilled via an LLM extractor). Initialized empty; not offline-induced and not a static external corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: memory items / experiences are embedded and retrieved by embedding-based similarity search (cosine/inner-product nearest-neighbor). No graph, hierarchy, or cluster organization (the paper deliberately keeps retrieval simple; modular/compositional and hierarchical organization are explicitly flagged as future work).
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based) retriever: semantic similarity search over memory embeddings. The paper uses Google Gemini text embeddings (cites Gemini Embedding, Lee et al. 2025; footnote 5 references https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings). Off-the-shelf, not learned.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf): retrieval is a fixed embedding-similarity top-k using pretrained Gemini embeddings; there is no contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback, RL, or downstream-task-effectiveness training of the retriever. The paper intentionally keeps retrieval simple to isolate the contribution of the reasoning-oriented memory CONTENT.
query_construction: Raw query context: the agent queries ReasoningBank with the current task query/context, embedded and matched against stored experiences via similarity search. No query decomposition, intent extraction, or synthetic query expansion.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): retrieval is performed once per incoming task query using the current query context, and retrieved memory items are injected into the agent's system instruction for the whole episode. Not per-step or per-state.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: memory retrieval happens once at the start of each task (top-k relevant experiences/items), then the agent runs its ReAct loop using the injected memory. There is no mid-episode iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered unconditionally at the beginning of every new task query (the agent queries ReasoningBank with the current query context). No token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated mid-episode trigger.
reranking: None. After embedding-similarity top-k retrieval, the retrieved experiences' memory items are injected directly into the system instruction; no cross-encoder, RRF, hierarchy-aware, or instruction-tuned reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at retrieval time: retrieved memory items are injected verbatim as additional system instructions without post-retrieval compression, decomposition, distillation, or distractor filtering. (Distillation/abstraction happens at WRITE time during memory extraction, not on the fetched items.) The k-ablation notes excessive retrieved experiences can introduce conflicts/noise, motivating a small k rather than a refinement stage.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: retrieved top-k memory items are injected into the agent's system instruction so that action prediction is grounded in past reasoning strategies, allowing the agent to recall effective insights and avoid previously observed pitfalls. No fine-tuning or latent-token injection; everything is in-context.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan, one-shot at plan time: relevant memory items are retrieved once per task and prepended to the system instruction; the agent then runs a ReAct (reason-act-observe) loop for the episode using that fixed memory context. No per-step re-retrieval, no MCTS/tree search inside the loop (default). MaTTS adds an outer test-time-scaling wrapper (parallel multi-rollout self-contrast or sequential self-refinement) around this retrieve-then-plan pipeline to generate richer experiences for memory curation.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-task (per-episode): retrieval and memory injection occur once before the ReAct rollout and remain fixed throughout the multi-step reasoning of that task. Not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy / structured note: a structured, human-interpretable and machine-usable memory item with title + one-sentence description + content (distilled reasoning steps, decision rationales, operational insights, or failure pitfalls/guardrails) in Markdown. Not a raw trajectory, executable program, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled high-level reasoning strategy / state-aware guideline. The memory schema deliberately abstracts away low-level execution details while preserving transferable reasoning patterns and strategies; the paper contrasts this against prior memory that stores raw trajectories (Synapse) or success-only procedural workflows (AWM). A case study shows items evolving from procedural action rules -> adaptive self-reflections -> adaptive checks -> compositional strategies over time.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) Self-verification via LLM-as-a-Judge to gate which trajectories are labeled success vs failure; the paper shows ReasoningBank is robust to judge noise: success rate is stable for simulated judge accuracy in the 70%-90% range (Figure 8). (2) Failure-aware extraction turns failed trajectories into corrective guardrails/pitfalls rather than noise. (3) Keeping retrieval k small (k=1 best) avoids conflicting/noisy retrieved context. (4) In MaTTS parallel scaling, self-contrast across multiple trajectories filters out spurious solutions and keeps consistent reasoning patterns.
memory_type: episodic-experience-derived strategy memory: a growing pool of distilled reasoning-strategy memory items (semantic/procedural knowledge) induced from the agent's episodic trajectories. Stored as plain structured text (title/description/content), not latent embeddings of content, not a graph.
write_back: Yes. After each task completes, the trajectory is processed by an LLM extraction pipeline (same backbone, temperature 1.0) that distills up to 3 structured memory items, which are then consolidated (added) into ReasoningBank, forming a closed-loop retrieve -> extract -> consolidate cycle.
online_growth: Yes. The memory store grows continuously during the streaming test-time deployment: starts empty and accumulates new memory items after every task, enabling sustained self-evolution (no offline freeze).
write_back_trigger: on-success-and-failure, per-task (reflective): after every completed task, an LLM-as-a-Judge assigns a proxy success/failure label, then memory items are extracted from BOTH successful trajectories (validated transferable strategies) and failed trajectories (counterfactual pitfalls / preventive guardrails) and appended. Writing is human-label-free (self-judged). In MaTTS, the abundant trajectories from scaling additionally feed contrastive memory curation.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure, contrastively used. Distinct from baselines (Synapse, AWM) that build memory only from successful trajectories: ReasoningBank extracts reasoning patterns from successes AND distills lessons/pitfalls/preventive strategies from failures. Ablation (Figure 7, WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash) shows adding failures raises ReasoningBank from 46.5 (success-only) to 49.7, whereas baselines stagnate or degrade (Synapse 40.6->41.7; AWM 44.4->42.2).
memory_evolution_update: append-only by default: memory consolidation is a 'simple addition' of newly extracted items into the pool with no pruning, merging, or overwriting (deliberately minimal to isolate the content contribution). Although individual stored strategies are observed to evolve in EFFECT over time via successive additions (emergent strategy refinement in the case study), the consolidation operator itself is append-only; merging/forgetting are flagged as future work.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Memory selection is fixed embedding-similarity top-k using off-the-shelf Gemini embeddings, not an RL- or value-optimized learned retrieval policy. (MaTTS scaling and the agent loop are not framed as a learned retrieval policy; the paper draws an analogy to RL learning dynamics but the retrieval itself is fixed similarity.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: one agent maintains and evolves its own ReasoningBank across the task stream. The work demonstrates cross-task / cross-website / cross-domain transfer of memory (e.g., Mind2Web cross-domain, WebArena Multi subset) but not sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: WebArena (684 instances across Shopping 187, Admin 182, Gitlab 180, Reddit 106, Multi 29; Map domain excluded due to website issues, following Miyai et al. 2025); Mind2Web (1341 instances: Cross-Task 252, Cross-Website 177, Cross-Domain 912); SWE-Bench-Verified (500 human-verified repository-level issue-resolution instances). Open-source-model study on WebArena-Shopping with Gemma-3-12B-Instruct.
benchmark_family: web (WebArena, Mind2Web) and code/software-engineering (SWE-Bench-Verified). No QA/multi-hop, embodied, or decision-RL benchmarks.
baselines: No Memory / Vanilla (backbone LLM agent, no memory); Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024, trajectory-as-exemplar in-context memory from successful trajectories); AWM = Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al. 2025d, abstracts reusable workflows/routines from successful trajectories). For SWE-Bench-Verified, only No Memory and Synapse are compared (AWM excluded because mini-SWE-Agent's open-ended bash action space precludes fixed workflows). MaTTS is also compared against vanilla TTS (test-time scaling without memory aggregation) and MaTTS-w/o-memory. All baselines share the SAME retrieval and consolidation; only the extraction (memory formulation) differs.
key_metrics: Web browsing: Success Rate (SR, %) for effectiveness and Average number of Steps (AS / Step) for efficiency on WebArena; Mind2Web reports Element Accuracy (EA), Action F1 (AF1), Step Success Rate (SSR), and task-level Success Rate (SR). SWE-Bench-Verified: issue Resolve/Resolution Rate (%) and Average Steps (AS). Scaling analyses report Pass@1, Best-of-N (BoN/Best-of-5), and Pass@k. Inference cost reported as average total token consumption per task.
headline_result: ReasoningBank consistently outperforms No-Memory, Synapse, and AWM across all backbones/datasets, with up to ~20% relative effectiveness improvement and up to 16% fewer interactions; MaTTS amplifies the gains. On WebArena overall SR it improves over memory-free agents by +8.3 (Gemini-2.5-flash 40.5->48.8), +7.2 (Gemini-2.5-pro 46.7->53.9), and +4.6 (Claude-3.7-sonnet 41.7->46.3); +MaTTS (parallel, k=5) further raises these (e.g., flash 48.8->51.8, pro 53.9->56.3, sonnet 46.3->48.8). On SWE-Bench-Verified, resolve rate rises from 34.2->38.8 (Gemini-2.5-flash) and 54.0->57.4 (Gemini-2.5-pro). The inference-cost study reports total tokens increase only ~4.3% over No-Memory while overall performance improves ~20.5%.
ablations: (1) Failure trajectories (Figure 7, WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash): ReasoningBank 46.5 (success-only) -> 49.7 (with failures), while Synapse 40.6->41.7 and AWM 44.4->42.2 (degrades), showing only ReasoningBank turns failures into constructive signals. (2) Number of retrieved experiences (Figure 13): k=1 best (49.7) vs No-Memory 39.0; SR declines with more retrieved items (46.0 at k=2, 45.5 at k=3, 44.4 at k=4), indicating relevance/quality over quantity. (3) MaTTS scaling factor k (Figures 4/5/14): parallel scaling 49.7 (k=1) -> 55.1 (k=5); sequential 49.7 -> 54.5; MaTTS w/o memory only fluctuates 39.0-42.2 (parallel) / 37.4-40.6 (sequential). (4) MaTTS vs vanilla TTS at k=5: 55.1 vs 52.4 (parallel), 54.5 vs 51.9 (sequential). (5) Memory-scaling synergy (Figure 5, BoN, k=5): BoN climbs from 49.7->55.1 with ReasoningBank vs No-Memory 39.0->42.2; Pass@1 rises 49.7->53.0 for ReasoningBank while weaker memories barely move (Synapse 40.6->41.2, AWM 44.4->45.5). (6) Judge-noise robustness (Figure 8): SR stable for simulated judge accuracy 70%-90%. (7) Step breakdown on successful vs failed cases (Table 4): larger step reductions on successful instances (up to 2.1 fewer, 26.9% relative). (8) Open-source model (Gemma-3-12B, Table 6): SR 17.1->24.1, fewest steps (11.8). (9) Inference cost (Table 5): ReasoningBank total ~53054 tokens vs No-Memory ~50847, Synapse ~58515, AWM ~59373.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (SR / resolve rate / EA / AF1 / SSR) plus efficiency (steps, tokens) and scaling metrics (Pass@1/BoN/Pass@k) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval completeness) are reported separately, since retrieval here is memory recall for prompting rather than a ranked-retrieval benchmark; the closest decoupled signal is the k-ablation on number of retrieved experiences.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mixed. Primary metrics are outcome-level (SR, resolve rate). The paper also reports process-relevant signals: efficiency via average interaction steps (overall and split by successful vs failed instances, Table 4), token-consumption breakdown (Table 5), Mind2Web step-level metrics (Step Success Rate, element accuracy, action F1), and qualitative analysis of emergent strategy evolution and per-step behavior in case studies.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strongly reported. Effectiveness gains come with reduced interaction steps (up to 1.4 fewer steps vs No-Memory and 1.6 vs other memory baselines on WebArena; 2.8/1.3 fewer steps on SWE-Bench; up to 16% fewer interactions overall). Token cost (Table 5): ReasoningBank ~53054 total tokens (Action 49306 + Judge 2186 + Extraction 1562) vs No-Memory 50847, Synapse 58515, AWM 59373 - i.e., only ~4.3% more tokens than No-Memory for ~20.5% performance gain, and CHEAPER than Synapse/AWM. MaTTS trades extra rollouts/refinement compute (scaling factor k up to 5) for higher SR and better Pass@k sample efficiency (e.g., 62.1 Pass@5 with MaTTS vs 52.4 without memory).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed small-k, budget-conscious: retrieve top-k relevant experiences/items (k=1 found best in the ablation; small k chosen because more retrieved items add conflict/noise). At most 3 memory items extracted per trajectory at write time. Web agents capped at 30 steps per query (BrowserGym). Retrieved items injected into the system instruction; no adaptive/precision-driven k or reranked-then-truncated budget cap beyond the small fixed k.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks: WebArena 684 instances over 5 domains with Map excluded; Mind2Web 1341 instances over cross-task/website/domain splits; SWE-Bench-Verified 500 human-verified instances). No new benchmark constructed.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (embedding-similarity top-k recall of past experiences/items), Reuse: yes (retrieved memory items injected into the system instruction to guide acting), Revise: partial (no per-case verbatim-then-adapt step; instead experiences are re-distilled and strategies evolve over the stream, and MaTTS self-contrast/self-refinement revises which strategies are curated), Retain: yes (new memory items extracted from successes and failures are consolidated/appended after every task)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as agent memory / experiential learning / self-evolving agents and test-time learning; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under memory and experience-learning framing (related to ExpeL, Synapse, AWM, AutoGuide).
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; the agent interacts with environments via BrowserGym web actions or bash commands, not a retrievable tool/API index).
index_content_separation: Partial: each memory item stores a lightweight title + one-sentence description for identification alongside heavier content (distilled reasoning steps). However, there is no progressive-disclosure mechanism that retrieves a light index first and loads heavy content on demand; retrieval returns whole items injected into the prompt.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or integration protocol such as MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful/function-calling; the memory store is an internally-managed growing pool, not a live external tool registry).
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted distillation/generalization rather than per-case verbatim reuse: an LLM extractor (temperature 1.0) converts each trajectory into up to 3 generalized strategy items; retrieved items are reused as injected guidance (not copied as a solution to be edited). MaTTS adds self-contrast (parallel) and self-refinement (sequential) to adapt which strategies are curated. No execution-feedback per-case revision of a single retrieved solution, no RL reuse-finetuning.
builds_on: Agent memory / experience-as-memory line: Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024) and AWM/Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al. 2025d) as the direct memory baselines extended; ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) agent loop; ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) and AutoGuide (Fu et al. 2024) for insight/guideline distillation; LLM-as-a-Judge (Gu et al. 2024) and autonomous trajectory evaluation (Pan et al. 2024) for self-verification; test-time scaling (Snell et al. 2025; Zhu et al. 2025), best-of-N (Chow et al. 2025), self-refine (Madaan et al. 2023), self-contrast/contrastive learning (Chen et al. 2020) for MaTTS; Gemini Embedding (Lee et al. 2025) for retrieval; BrowserGym (de Chezelles et al. 2025) and mini-SWE-Agent (Yang et al. 2024) execution environments. Code adapts agent-workflow-memory, webarena, and mini-swe-agent repos.
contrasts_with: Memory mechanisms that store RAW trajectories (Synapse, RAP/Kagaya 2024, MapAgent) or SUCCESS-ONLY procedural workflows/routines/skills (AWM, Memp/Fang 2025, skill-set optimization/Nottingham 2024, ICE/Qian 2024) and instance-level concepts (Dynamic Cheatsheet, ExpeL) - ReasoningBank instead stores distilled high-level reasoning strategies and learns from BOTH successes and failures. Also contrasts with vanilla test-time scaling that ignores memory (Zhu et al. 2025; ExACT/Yu 2025b; Thinking-vs-Doing/Shen 2025; multi-agent TTS/Jin 2025), which MaTTS shows is suboptimal without memory-aware aggregation.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience planning): a 2025-2026 self-evolving agent-memory method advancing the ExpeL -> Synapse -> AWM -> AutoGuide lineage of experience/insight memory. Its distinctive contributions are (a) storing distilled, transferable REASONING STRATEGIES (not raw trajectories or success-only workflows), (b) learning from FAILURES via self-judged contrastive signals in a label-free streaming test-time-learning setting, and (c) introducing memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS) that couples memory curation with inference-time compute scaling as a new scaling dimension for self-evolving agents.
